Papyri: Elephantine (Berlin ERC database, 799 documents, 19,903 fully legible words) and ten Arshama letters (1,040 words); only fully legible words counted. Targums: Onkelos (Pentateuch, 82,706 words) and Jonathan (Joshua–Kings, Isaiah, 94,519 words) from Sefaria. Every hit is listed with its reference in the project files. Mt Gerizim inscriptions (3rd–2nd c. BCE): zy 32 / dy 9, znh 2 / dnh 5, causative h- 24 / ʾ- 0.
imp_limit: The Persian-era Aramaic is mostly letters, contracts and accounts from one Egyptian garrison. The Wadi Daliyeh, Bactrian and Persepolis Aramaic texts are not openly available, and the Comprehensive Aramaic Lexicon asks not to be scraped (it offers data dumps on request).
